questionText:

Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen oversaw the colossal logistical exercise. Over 17.3 crore eligible voters had to be registered, 85 percent of whom could neither read nor write. To overcome mass illiteracy, the Election Commission assigned distinctive symbols to candidates and placed separate ballot boxes for each candidate inside polling booths. The elections, held between October 1951 and February 1952, saw enthusiastic voter turnout, including millions of women. The fair and peaceful conduct of the polls silenced critics, proving that democracy could flourish in conditions of poverty and illiteracy."
